## Errors already occurring

## Limits of this evidence
- Data covers one member account. The org-level trail `all-trails-of-org-level` (in the management account) was not read, so cross-account callers into this account are not visible. Calls from other member accounts would not show here, and I did not check S3 trail logs.

- Invocation logging is region-specific. It showed no activity outside us-east-1, but I did not confirm logging is enabled in other regions.
- I did not find EC2, ECS or EKS workloads calling Bedrock. The only ECS-EC2 evidence is CodeBuild's own runtime. I did not enumerate every EC2 instance profile or the IAM policies that grant `bedrock:*`.
- The Bedrock API key user showed no calls. Bedrock API-key calls would show as that IAM user in CloudTrail.
- A deny on `bedrock:*` does not cover `bedrock-agentcore:*`, `aoss:*` and similar actions. If the SCP only denies the bedrock service prefixes, AgentCore runtime and gateway calls are unaffected, though their Bedrock model calls are not.

## Suggested follow-ups
1. Check the management account's org trail (S3 or CloudWatch Logs) for cross-account Bedrock callers.
2. Page eu-west-1 and us-east-1 CloudTrail back to the 90-day edge for rarer events (`InvokeAgent`, `Retrieve`, `CreateModelCustomizationJob`, `CreateGuardrail`).
3. Audit IAM policies and instance profiles that allow `bedrock:*`, plus any VPC endpoint (`vpce-...`) paths used by the KB roles.
4. Decide how to carve out the DevOps Agent role and Knowledge Base service roles, for example with an SCP condition on `aws:PrincipalArn`."}]}], "label": "Sub-agent "bedrock-usage-activity""}

{"id": "ccee8a88-874a-4d0b-908b-fe1f0b184e92", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_tTF337e6j7nMvfeQotSIaw", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"Find the changes that could explain the symptoms, or confirm whether and when a specific change happened.\\\\n\\\\n## CloudTrail: `lookup_cloudtrail_events`\\\\n\\\\nCloudTrail calls through `use_aws` are blocked; `lookup_cloudtrail_events` is the route. It returns management events from the last 90 days, newest first, for one account and region per call.\\\\n\\\\n- Each call returns at most about 10,000 characters of events. Every event carries its full CloudTrailEvent JSON, so a call often holds only a handful of events. When it stops early it returns `continuation_timestamp`; pass that as the next `end_time` to page to older events.\\\\n- With no attribute, the tool returns only write events (`ReadOnly` is `false`), which is what a change timeline needs. LookupEvents takes one attribute per call, so passing `attribute_key` and `attribute_value` (EventSource, ResourceName, Username, EventName and so on) replaces that default, and read-only calls then share the size cap with the writes. Use an attribute to follow one resource, user or event name.\\\\n- Narrow before you page: exclude noisy event names and use windows of about 15 minutes. Excluded events do not count toward the size cap. `jmespath_filter` runs after the cap, so it shrinks the output but does not return more events.\\\\n- Passing `exclude_event_names` replaces the default exclusions (`CreateLogStream`, `Invoke`, `InvokeExecution`, `UpdateInstanceInformation`, `PutObject`); include them again if you still want them dropped.\\\\n- LookupEvents allows 2 requests per second per account and region, and one tool call may page several times, so run at most 2 CloudTrail calls at once.\\\\n- Start near the symptom onset and work backward until you find changes that address the question or have covered the requested timeframe.\\\\n\\\\nKubernetes events come from `use_kubectl`. RDS `describe_events` covers only the last 14 days; for an older window, use CloudTrail.\\\\n\\\\n## Judging a change\\\\n\\\\nA change during the incident window matters only if it relates to the investigative question or explains a symptom. When a change modified a resource that is now degraded, describe the resulting state, not just the event, and say whether that state deterministically stops the resource from working (an emptied security group, revoked IAM permissions, a black-hole route). A deterministic block takes precedence over load-based explanations, and timing alone is no reason to dismiss it.\\\\n\\\\nStop when the question is settled: you have found changes that address it, or you have covered the requested timeframe without finding any, in which case say what you searched.\\\\n\\\\nRecord each relevant change with `write_activity_observation`, including the event count and the timespan covered, unless your instructions have you state findings in your own reasoning instead.\", \"resource_manifest\": [\"references/azure.md\"]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_zS4B3LlfhB7ji2XHaWMdV0", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"Find the metric evidence that answers the investigative question, comparing the incident window with a healthy baseline. If you were delegated a scope, stay within it: resources mentioned only as background are not in scope.\\\\n\\\\n## CloudWatch\\\\n\\\\nQuery with `use_aws` `cloudwatch` `get_metric_data`. The period must fit CloudWatch retention: for a window that starts more than 15 days ago use a multiple of 300 seconds, and more than 63 days ago a multiple of 3600 seconds; a shorter period returns no data points. Details: [./references/cloudwatch-retention.md](./references/cloudwatch-retention.md). Each `MetricDataQueries` `Id` must start with a lowercase letter. A request may hold at most one Metrics Insights `SELECT`; a second one fails with \\\\\"Maximum number of queries (1) exceeded\\\\\". The request can still retrieve other metrics, and math expressions can use the `SELECT`\\'s result. If you fall back to `get_metric_statistics`, it returns at most 1,440 data points per call.\\\\n\\\\nPromQL (`get_prometheus_metrics`, enabled by reading [./references/cloudwatch-promql.md](./references/cloudwatch-promql.md)) serves AWS-vended metrics with OTel enrichment, whose series carry the resource ARN and resource tags as labels. An account without enriched metrics returns empty results; use `get_metric_data` there.\\\\n\\\\n## RDS and Aurora: Performance Insights\\\\n\\\\nPerformance Insights (PI) shows database load by wait event and by SQL statement, which CloudWatch cannot. Start with `db.load.avg`; where load is elevated, group by `db.wait_event` and `db.sql_tokenized`.\\\\n- In `describe_dimension_keys`, leave `AdditionalMetrics` out unless you need it: names such as `db.sql_tokenized.stats.*` are not known on every engine. `get_dimension_key_details` does not accept the `db.sql_tokenized` group; its error lists the groups the engine supports.\\\\n\\\\nRequest shapes and the period limits PI enforces: [./references/rds-performance-insights.md](./references/rds-performance-insights.md).\\\\n\\\\nStop when the question is settled: an anomaly has been checked against the baseline, or the window shows nothing beyond baseline noise, in which case say what you queried.\\\\n\\\\n## Recording findings\\\\n\\\\nRecord each noteworthy data point with `write_metric_observation` unless your instructions have you state findings in your own reasoning instead.\", \"resource_manifest\": [\"references/azure.md\", \"references/cloudwatch-promql.md\", \"references/cloudwatch-retention.md\", \"references/datadog.md\", \"references/dynatrace.md\", \"references/grafana.md\", \"references/newrelic.md\", \"references/rds-performance-insights.md\", \"references/splunk.md\"]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_pPPUh53TSznbOU79tbAhgT", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"Find the log evidence that answers the investigative question, and check each candidate against a healthy baseline window before treating it as incident-related.\\\\n\\\\n## CloudWatch Logs\\\\n\\\\nQuery with `query_cloudwatch_logs` rather than `use_aws` (`start_query` with `get_query_results`, or `filter_log_events`). It runs one Logs Insights query against one log group and polls for about 30 seconds; a query still running after that returns an error, so narrow the time range or the filter and retry.\\\\n\\\\nA tool result larger than about 10K tokens (roughly 35K characters) is replaced by a short preview. Keep `limit` small (5 to 20) when you return raw records, and use `stats` or `pattern` to look at volume.\\\\n\\\\nLogs Insights details that are easy to get wrong:\\\\n- `sort` cannot take a function call such as `count()` or `bin(1m)`; alias it in `stats` and sort on the alias: `stats count() as n by bin(1m) as t | sort t`.\\\\n- Compare `@timestamp` with a number only inside `filter`; in `fields`, `stats` or `by` the comparison is a type mismatch.\\\\n- Convert times with the `datetime` tool rather than by hand; hand-computed Unix seconds can be a whole year off.\\\\n- A query whose window ends before a log group was created fails with \\\\\"end date is before the log group\\'s creation time\\\\\". `describe_log_groups` shows each group\\'s `creationTime`, so list an unfamiliar set of groups before querying it.\\\\n- `pattern @message | anomaly` groups messages into patterns and keeps only the statistically unusual ones, which makes it a cheap first look at a busy log group. `pattern` cannot be combined with `stats`.\\\\n- In a regex, `|` means OR, so `(error|500)` matches every \\\\\"500\\\\\" in timestamps and IDs. Match status codes in context, for example `status[:\\\\\\\\s]*\\\\\\\\b5\\\\\\\\d{2}\\\\\\\\b`.\\\\n- A `stats count() by bin(1m)` query over a range that spans the baseline and the incident compares a pattern\\'s frequency in one call.\\\\n\\\\nMore query patterns: [./references/query-examples.md](./references/query-examples.md).\\\\n\\\\n## Baseline and stopping\\\\n\\\\nA pattern that is about as frequent in a healthy window as in the incident window is pre-existing noise, not an incident signal. {"id": "a3840862-882a-48e1-902d-a033dc96b471", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**Scope:** I only had access to account 123456789012, which is a member account. The management account is 111122223333. The inventory is for this one account, not the whole org.

## Summary
- Bedrock is in active use in this account. About 22.9k invocations are logged between 2026-10-15 and 2026-11-20. Almost all of it is us-east-1. Anything that calls Bedrock through a role or user in a member account will stop working under the SCP.
- Real invocation traffic is concentrated in four groups: human Admin SSO sessions, CodeBuild eval jobs, Lambda test and eval apps, and Knowledge Base service roles.
- The DevOps Agent's own role also calls Bedrock continuously, but only read APIs.

## Evidence used
- **CloudTrail management events.** Here, Bedrock `Converse`, `InvokeModel` and `ConverseStream` calls are recorded as management events, so `lookup_cloudtrail_events` shows them. There are no data-event selectors on the account trail.
- **Bedrock model invocation logging.** Logging is on, delivering to the log group `/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations` in us-east-1. It holds 22,889 records from 2026-10-15 onward, and I used it for per-principal counts, first/last seen and error codes.
- **CloudWatch `AWS/Bedrock`.** Used to corroborate volume, and to check other regions.

## Principals that call Bedrock
All are in us-east-1 unless noted. Counts come from the invocation log (Oct 15–Nov 20).

| Principal | Type / workload | Actions | Calls | First – last seen | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assumed-role/Admin`, 7 sessions: user-d 3,557; user-a 2,763; user-c-AgenticAccess 2,647; user-e 1,904; user-b 1,324; user-f 288; user-g 1 | Humans via AccountMgmt role | `Converse` (12.3k), `ConverseStream` (187, user-a) | ~12.5k | 10-16 – **11-20 03:48** | user-a is still active now, via the Kiro IDE. The user agent is Boto3 with `app/kiro-ide`. |
| `user/llmops-demo-admin` | IAM user (1 active access key, created 10-15) | `Converse` 3,926; `InvokeModel` 2 | 3,928 | 10-15 – 11-07 | User agent is Boto3 with `app/kiro-ide`, from a home IP (49.207.216.85). |
| `assumed-role/llmops-eval-runner` (49 sessions) | CodeBuild project `llmops-eval-runner` | `Converse` | ~5,000 | 10-26 – 11-17 | Boto3 on ECS-EC2 (CodeBuild). Bursty batch runs. |
| `llmops-lf-*` app roles (~45 roles, one session each): `-app-*`, `-gr-*`, `-gh-*`, `-aip`, `-catalog-*`, `-agent-ondemand`, `-mkt-probe` | Lambda test apps (`inScopeOf` AWS::Lambda::Function) | `Converse`, `ConverseStream`, `InvokeModel` | ~1.3k combined | 11-05 – 11-16 | The Lambda functions no longer exist. Only the roles remain. |
| `assumed-role/llmops-lf-kbrole` (128 sessions, `BKB-*` names) and `llmops-demo-kb-role` (25 calls, last 11-04) | Bedrock Knowledge Base service role (`invokedBy bedrock.amazonaws.com`) | `InvokeModel` (embeddings, titan-embed-text-v2) | 172 and 25 | 10-15 – 11-16 | These are service-initiated calls using the customer role. An SCP deny applies to them, so KB ingest and Retrieve would break. |
| `llmops-lf-kbrole-noread` | Test KB role | `InvokeModel` | 3 | 11-05 – 11-16 | |
| `assumed-role/llmops-demo-sagemaker-exec` | SageMaker | `Converse` | 175 | 10-18 only | |
| `assumed-role/AgentCoreRole-cost_estimator_agent` | AgentCore runtime | `ConverseStream` | 2 | 10-15 – 10-22 | |
| `DevOpsAgentRole-AgentSpace-8a62f606ec14` (session `monitorAssociationRoleSession`) | AWS DevOps Agent | Read only: `GetGuardrail`, `ListTagsForResource`, `GetKnowledgeBase`, `GetAgentRuntime`, `GetModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration`, `ListAgents`, `ListEvaluationJobs`. It also called `ListFoundationModels` a few times. | Continuous | Through 11-20 03:50 | It runs in us-east-1, us-west-2 and us-east-2. An SCP deny would break the agent's visibility into Bedrock. |
| `llmops-lf-app-wrongregion-role` (Lambda `llmops-lf-app-wrongregion`) | Lambda, **eu-west-1** | `Converse` | ~4 per day | At least 11-11 – 11-16 | Every call fails with `ValidationException` (invalid model ID), so it isn't useful traffic. I did not page back to its first day. |
| `user/llmops-lf-apikey-user` | IAM user with a Bedrock API key (expires 12-05) | none seen | 0 | n/a | No calls found. The key is created but unused. |
| `resource-explorer-2` | Service principal | `ListKnowledgeBases` (us-east-2) | 1 seen | 11-14 | Control-plane listing. |

## Model usage
- Records by model: Claude Sonnet 5 13.9k, gpt-5.6-terra 7.1k, Nova Lite 1.1k, Titan embeddings ~200, Opus 4.8 187.
- CloudWatch over the last 30 days shows Sonnet 5 at about 8.2k invocations and about 10.5k more under "Other".

## Errors already occurring
- **No SCP-style AccessDenied is occurring.**
- The 64 `AccessDeniedException` records come from `llmops-lf-gr-noperm-app-role` and `llmops-lf-gr-xregion-app-role` (32 each, 11-05 to 11-16). They look like deliberate negative tests of missing IAM permission.
- Other errors are `ValidationException` (bad model IDs, about 300) and a few `ModelErrorException` and `InternalServerException`. They are not access-related.
- I did not search CloudTrail for denied events in other regions or for non-Converse event names.

## Other regions
- **us-west-2, us-east-2, eu-central-1, ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-1:** `AWS/Bedrock` metrics are empty. CloudTrail shows no `Converse` or `InvokeModel` events in the regions I checked (`InvokeModel` in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 only).
- us-west-2 and us-east-2 show only the DevOps Agent role's read calls.
- **eu-west-1:** only the `wrongregion` Lambda above.
- Other regions might have activity, but I only checked these seven. CloudTrail does not cover regions I did not query.

## Other Bedrock-related resources
- **AgentCore:** runtimes (`llmops_eval_*`, `cost_estimator_agent`), a gateway, and a CodeBuild builder exist. The `bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com` event source also shows the DevOps Agent role's reads.
- **EventBridge:** `llmops-eval-synthetic-traffic` (every 5 minutes) is **DISABLED**. `llmops-eval-config-rollout` is also DISABLED. `llmops-lf-daily` is ENABLED at 06:00 UTC, but its target Lambda `llmops-lf-trigger` no longer exists.
- **Invocation logging:** the role `llmops-demo-bedrock-logging` (trusted by `bedrock.amazonaws.com`) delivers the logs.
- **Roles trusted by `bedrock.amazonaws.com`:** `llmops-demo-eval-role`, `llmops-demo-kb-role`, `llmops-lf-kbrole`, `llmops-lf-custom-svc`. These would be affected for Knowledge Base, evaluation and similar service calls.

## Limits of this evidence
- Data covers one member account. The org-level trail `all-trails-of-org-level` (in the management account) was not read, so cross-account callers into this account are not visible. Calls from other member accounts would not show here, and I did not check S3 trail logs.
- The CloudTrail lookup returns only a few events per page, so I used it for sampling and discovery. Volume figures come from the invocation log, and that log only runs from 2026-10-15 (the log group was created then), so earlier traffic isn't covered.
- Invocation logging is region-specific. It showed no activity outside us-east-1, but I did not confirm logging is enabled in other regions.
- I did not find EC2, ECS or EKS workloads calling Bedrock. The only ECS-EC2 evidence is CodeBuild's own runtime. I did not enumerate every EC2 instance profile or the IAM policies that grant `bedrock:*`.
- The Bedrock API key user showed no calls. Bedrock API-key calls would show as that IAM user in CloudTrail.
- A deny on `bedrock:*` does not cover `bedrock-agentcore:*`, `aoss:*` and similar actions. If the SCP only denies the bedrock service prefixes, AgentCore runtime and gateway calls are unaffected, though their Bedrock model calls are not.

## Suggested follow-ups
1. Check the management account's org trail (S3 or CloudWatch Logs) for cross-account Bedrock callers.
2. Page eu-west-1 and us-east-1 CloudTrail back to the 90-day edge for rarer events (`InvokeAgent`, `Retrieve`, `CreateModelCustomizationJob`, `CreateGuardrail`).
3. Audit IAM policies and instance profiles that allow `bedrock:*`, plus any VPC endpoint (`vpce-...`) paths used by the KB roles.
4. Decide how to carve out the DevOps Agent role and Knowledge Base service roles, for example with an SCP condition on `aws:PrincipalArn`.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

For a resource found in a failed or degraded state, record the resource itself (name, type, connections) and leave out its health.\", \"resource_manifest\": [\"references/aws.md\", \"references/azure.md\"]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_wEJboDNlQpmh6LSwZRhTvL", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"# Exploring Code\\\\n\\\\nSearch and analyze code repositories to find implementations, understand project structure, and examine code changes in specific git commits.\\\\n\\\\n## Specialization\\\\n\\\\nYou are now specialized in searching and analyzing existing the user\\'s code repositories. You excel at:\\\\n- Rapidly finding files using glob patterns\\\\n- Searching code and text with powerful regex patterns\\\\n- Reading and analyzing file contents to match the user\\'s intent\\\\n\\\\n## Guidelines\\\\n\\\\n- Use `list_repositories` to discover code repository details enabled by the user\\\\n- Use `repo_glob` for broad file pattern matching\\\\n- Use `repo_grep` for searching file contents with regex\\\\n- Use `repo_ls` for discovering the structure of the repository\\\\n- Use `repo_read` when you know the specific file path you need to read\\\\n- Use `git_diff` without a `base_ref` to achieve \\\\\"git show\\\\\" and display the content of a git commit:\\\\n  ```\\\\n  git_diff(\\\\n      repository=\\\\\"owner/repo\\\\\",\\\\n      hostname=\\\\\"github.com\\\\\",\\\\n      target_ref=\\\\\"a922cd1026c5d2f298dc5f83951f58f592ae6646\\\\\"\\\\n  )\\\\n  ```\\\\n- The `repo_*` tools can be used in conjunction with `git_diff` to explore additional files in the git tree outside of the diff\\\\n\\\\nYou are meant to be a fast agent that returns output as quickly as possible on whether target git commits matched the user\\'s prompt.\\\\n- Make efficient use of the tools that you have at your disposal: be smart about how you search for files and implementations\\\\n- Wherever possible you should try to spawn multiple parallel tool calls for grepping and reading files\\\\n\\\\n## Output format\\\\n\\\\nHere is a sensible format, but use your judgement:\\\\n\\\\n````md\\\\nSUMMARY:\\\\n[3-5 sentences summarizing what you explored and what you found or didn\\'t find]\\\\n\\\\nFINDINGS:\\\\n\\\\n```xml\\\\n<findings>\\\\n  <finding id=\\\\\"[short-descriptive-id]\\\\\">\\\\n    <repository hostname=\\\\\"[git hostname]\\\\\" name=\\\\\"[owner/repo]\\\\\" ref=\\\\\"[branch, tag, or commit]\\\\\" />\\\\n    <description>[Brief explanation (3-5 sentences) of what was found and why it is relevant to the task]</description>\\\\n\\\\n    <!-- Use the appropriate reference type(s) for the finding. All are optional \\\\u2014 include only what\\'s relevant. -->\\\\n\\\\n    <!-- For code locations found via repo_grep, repo_read -->\\\\n    <code_references>\\\\n      <reference>\\\\n        <file path=\\\\\"[file path relative to repo root]\\\\\" lines=\\\\\"[start-end, if applicable]\\\\\" />\\\\n        <content>\\\\n        [Relevant code snippet or summary]\\\\n        </content>\\\\n      </reference>\\\\n      <!-- Additional code references -->\\\\n    </code_references>\\\\n\\\\n    <!-- For code changes found via git_diff -->\\\\n    <diff_references>\\\\n      <diff from=\\\\\"[base ref]\\\\\" to=\\\\\"[target ref]\\\\\">\\\\n        <file path=\\\\\"[file path]\\\\\" status=\\\\\"[added|modified|deleted|renamed]\\\\\" additions=\\\\\"[count]\\\\\" deletions=\\\\\"[count]\\\\\" />\\\\n        <content>\\\\n        [Relevant diff snippet]\\\\n        </content>\\\\n      </diff>\\\\n      <!-- Additional diffs -->\\\\n    </diff_references>\\\\n\\\\n    <!-- For structural findings from repo_ls, repo_glob, list_repositories -->\\\\n    <details>\\\\n      [Freeform description of structural findings, directory layouts, file lists, etc.]\\\\n    </details>\\\\n  </finding>\\\\n  <!-- Additional findings -->\\\\n</findings>\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nEXPLORED BUT NOT RELEVANT:\\\\n* [What was searched]: [why dismissed in < 20 words]\\\\n\\\\nUNABLE TO EXPLORE:\\\\n* [What couldn\\'t be accessed]: [error or reason]\\\\n````\\\\n\\\\n### Output guidelines\\\\n\\\\n- Include only findings that are relevant to the task\\\\n- Use the reference type that best fits the data\\\\n- Keep code snippets and diffs focused \\\\u2014 include enough context to be useful, not entire files\\\\n- When referencing files, always include the repository and ref for clarity\\\\n- If findings span multiple repositories, group by repository\"}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

Several findings affect what the SCP must cover:
- An SCP on `bedrock:*` does not cover `bedrock-agentcore:*`. AgentCore uses a separate IAM prefix. Decide whether to deny it too.
- Several Bedrock paths run through service principals or service roles (knowledge bases, model invocation logging, evaluation). An SCP applies to those roles too.

## 1. IAM
